What is the virtual contract note, and how to view it? - The virtual contract note provides an approximation of brokerage, STT, stamp duty, exchange transaction charges, SEBI turnover charge, and GST for the day. It also provides order-wise charges, unlike a regular contract note. To view it on the Kite app, tap Orders, then Executed, then Contract note. On Kite web, click Orders, then Contract note.  Note: The virtual contract note does not display the additional brokerage of ₹40 charged when the Zerodha account has a negative balance; DP charges are levied separately on the funds statement; for NRI and Non-individual accounts, the brokerage charge displayed isn't calculated as per the actual rate; and it functions for up to 500 executed orders.  For more than 500, refer to the contract note sent to the registered email.

How to understand the contract note? - A contract note is the legal record of all transactions through stockbrokers on stock exchanges, including all trades executed on a particular day.  They're sent to the registered email on the trade date and can be downloaded from Console. The format changed August 1, 2024.  The first page shows broker and client information, trade date, settlement date, etc. The next page shows segment (equity, derivatives), ISIN, quantities, WAP, and brokerage details.  WAP (Weighted Average Price) is calculated differently for equity and derivatives (formulas provided in the text). The following page displays obligation details: pay-in/pay-out obligations (in brackets if payable, otherwise receivable); applicable brokerages and taxes (GST, STT, stamp duty, SEBI turnover fee, exchange transaction tax) are displayed; and the net amount receivable or payable. Annexure A (on the next page) includes trade details (Order No., Order time, Trade No., Trade time, Security/Contract description, Buy(B)/Sell(S), Exchange, Quantity, Gross Rate/Trade Price Per unit, Brokerage per Unit, Net Rate per unit, Closing Rate per unit (derivatives only), Net total (Before Levies), Remarks). Other charges (call and trade, DP charges) are on the funds statement, not the contract note.  Order and Trade numbers in the format 111111 or 222222 indicate exchange settlement; 333333 indicates physical settlement.  The format of contract notes changed on August 1, 2024; older formats may be displayed for dates prior to this.

Are the F&O positions settled on the exchange on the expiry day displayed on the contract notes? - Yes.  Open F&O contracts held until expiry and settled on the exchange are displayed. Order no. and Trade no. are displayed as 111111 (options) or 222222 (futures) to indicate exchange settlement; 333333 indicates physical settlement. Order time is 15:40:00, trade time is 00:00:00. The Gross Rate/Trade Price Per unit is the exchange settlement price.

Why is the contract note delayed or not delivered? - Contract note delivery may be delayed if the exchanges delay sending trade files to Zerodha.  Generally, they're sent to the client's registered email on the trade date, but processing time depends on when Zerodha receives the files from the exchanges.  Contract notes can also be downloaded from Console.

How to view or download the profit and loss report? - To view or download the P&L report, go to console.zerodha.com/reports/pnl, select the segment, choose Combined, Realised, or Unrealised P&L, select the date range, and click View.  The report can then be downloaded as a spreadsheet.  Note: Zerodha provides no warranty for the authenticity and completeness of the data; clients should cross-check it with their tradebook, contract notes, and funds statement.

How to change the date format of Console reports? - Download the report in CSV format, select the date column, right-click and select Format Cells, click Date, then Custom, and enter the desired format.

How to get the trade and P&L reports for a period before FY 2017-18? - Trade and P&L reports have been available on Console only since FY 2017-18. To obtain data for earlier periods, create a ticket to request the trade book, contract notes, or ledger.  Clients can manually prepare P&L reports for earlier periods using the trade book and contract notes.

What does the profit and loss heat-map on Console represent? - The profit and loss heat map on Console visually displays daily gross profit and loss (P&L) reports. Green indicates profit, red indicates loss; lighter shades show smaller amounts, darker shades show larger amounts.  The value displayed when hovering over a tile is the gross realised P&L for that day.

What do 'Other credits & debits' in the Console P&L report mean? -  The "Other credits & debits" entry in the Console P&L report refers to charges and credits not directly related to trading activities, excluding brokerage, exchange transaction charges, STT, GST, stamp duty, and SEBI charges (which are on the contract note and funds statement).  This includes call and trade charges, payment gateway charges, DP charges, account opening charges, margin penalty, delayed payment charges, AMC charges, and more.  A breakdown is available in the Tax P&L and the second sheet of the downloaded P&L report.

Why does Kite P&L not match with credit/debit on Console? - Kite (trading platform) and Console (back office) calculate P&L differently, though the overall P&L is consistent. Kite's futures and options position page uses FIFO (First In, First Out) for P&L based on the entry price. Console settles P&L daily using M2M (Marked to Market) for futures positions.  Kite shows overall and current day P&L; Console's ledger shows multiple daily entries, but the overall P&L totals match.

What could be the reason for a profit and loss report to appear incorrect? - An incorrect P&L report may be due to corporate actions (bonus, splits, rights issues, mergers, spin-offs, buybacks, etc.), discrepant quantities entered for off-market share transfers or IPOs, or short delivery/auction scenarios.  If any of these apply, create a ticket.

How to download the tax P&L or capital gains statement at Zerodha? - On Console, click Reports, then Tax P&L, select the financial year and quarter range, click the arrow, and then click "Download Tax P&L report for all segments" at the bottom to download the report.

How to check capital gains applicability on the current holdings? - The "View breakdown" option in holdings shows purchase date, quantity, price, age (days since purchase), and P&L.  LTCG (Long-Term Capital Gains) applies to holdings over 365 days; STCG (Short-Term Capital Gains) applies to holdings under 365 days.  To view this information: On the Kite app, tap Portfolio, select the stock, and tap View breakdown. On Kite Web, click Holdings, click Options, and select View breakdown. On Console, click Portfolio, then Holdings, then Options, and select View breakdown/tags.  For more information on market-related taxation, visit zerodha.com/varsity/module/markets-and-taxation.


How is turnover calculated in Tax P&L and how can one determine the need for an audit? - Zerodha uses the turnover calculation on Console to determine if a tax audit is needed, following the guidance note on tax audit under section 44AB.  Turnover is calculated as follows: Delivery: sell-side value; Intraday: absolute sum of profits and losses per stock; F&O (equity, currency, commodity): absolute sum of profits and losses per contract. Note: There may be differences in turnover calculations between the tradewise and segments sheets on the downloaded Tax P&L report; use the tradewise turnover for tax filing.



How are the dividends on Liquid ETFs and Liquid BeES taxed? - Dividends on Liquid ETFs and Liquid BeES are taxed at the investor's income tax slab rate.  When sold, the dividend value is the cost of acquisition, and any gains are taxed under capital gains (STCG if sold within 3 years, taxed at slab rates; LTCG if held over 3 years, taxed at 12.5% with the first ₹1,25,000 exempt). For purchases after April 1, 2023, all gains are short-term and taxed at the investor's slab rate.  If dividends exceed ₹5,000, an additional 10% TDS applies.  Consult a chartered accountant for tax filing assistance.

What are Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) and Short-Term Capital gains (STCG), and how are they calculated? - Capital gains are profits from selling assets (stocks, bonds, real estate, etc.), the difference between selling and purchase prices.  LTCG (Long-Term Capital Gains) applies to assets held for a specified period (usually over 1 year).  Before July 23rd, 2024, LTCG on securities was taxed at 10%; after that date, it's 12.5%. The LTCG exemption limit is ₹1,25,000 per year (from FY 2024-25). A grandfathering clause allows using the asset's January 31, 2018 price for LTCG calculations for some assets. STCG (Short-Term Capital Gains) applies to assets held for one year or less. Before July 23rd, 2024, STCG on securities was taxed at 15%; after that date, it's 20%.  There's no exemption for STCG.  Specific tax rates for LTCG and STCG vary by asset type and holding period (tables provided in the text).  Download the Tax P&L report for LTCG tax liability.

Who is liable to pay taxes on the P&L in a joint demat account? - The primary or first holder of the joint demat account is liable for taxes on the profit and loss.

Why are the returns on liquid ETFs like Liquidbees, DSP Liquid ETF, and ICICI Liquid ETF lesser than the returns displayed on their websites? - Before the 2020 budget, liquid ETFs had a 28.84% Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT), deducted before distributing dividends. Website returns didn't account for this.  After the budget, DDT was removed; dividends are now taxed at the investor's income tax slab rate (plus an additional 10% TDS if dividends exceed ₹5,000).

What should be done when an income tax notice is received? - After filing Income Tax Returns (ITR), you may receive a notice (sections 139(9), 143(1), or 143(1)(a)). Contact Quicko (WEB), Zerodha's tax planning and filing partner, for guidance on handling such notices.

How to view the long-term and short-term holdings separately? - Console's "Tags" feature allows tagging securities as long-term (held over 1 year) or short-term (held under 1 year).  Use Console filters to view them separately.  See "How to add tags on Zerodha’s Console?" for instructions. Note:  Holdings can't be sold separately; the FIFO (First-In-First-Out) method is used for tax purposes, regardless of how holdings are viewed.  The investor is responsible for indicating short-term or long-term capital gains/losses when filing taxes.



Can input tax credit be claimed on the GST paid for Zerodha's service? - Yes, if the services are used for business purposes (not by a retail investor) and the GST registration is linked to the demat account's PAN. To add your GST number to contract notes and invoices, provide your GST registration certificate by creating a ticket.  See "How to download the GST invoice for the charges posted on the funds statement?" for instructions.

What is tax loss harvesting? - Tax-loss harvesting is selling losing securities to offset capital gains taxes. For example, if you have ₹100,000 in short-term capital gains (taxed at 15%) and ₹60,000 in unrealized losses, selling the losing stocks reduces your taxable gains to ₹40,000, saving you taxes.  While not explicitly disallowed in India, consult a CA before using this strategy, as it may be questioned by tax authorities if the same stock is quickly repurchased.  A tax-loss harvesting report is available at console.zerodha.com/reports/tax-loss-harvesting/eq.  For more information, see zerodha.com/varsity/module/markets-and-taxation/ and zrd.sh/tax-loss-harvesting-22.  Note: Console uses FIFO (First In First Out) for buy average and P&L; selling a stock to harvest losses may also realize long-term capital gains; the first ₹100,000 of long-term gains is tax-free and not considered in the report; and there's no harvesting opportunity if losses exceed profits.

Where can the holding period of investments and the tax liability based on the grandfather clause of LTCG be found? - The tax liability for long-term stock investments (under the grandfather clause) is in the Tradewise Tax P&L report on Console. This report shows entry and exit dates and holding period information. See "How to download the tax P&L or capital gains statement at Zerodha?" for download instructions.



What does the Trade book heat map on Console represent? - The trade book heat map visually represents the trade book using color-coding to show the number of trades; lighter colors mean fewer trades, darker colors mean more trades.  It helps identify trading/investing patterns to improve strategy.  View it at console.zerodha.com/reports/tradebook; select the segment and duration to update the heat map.  Clicking a tile shows the number and details of trades for that day.



What is an Annual Information Statement (AIS)? - An Annual Information Statement (AIS) is a report on the income tax portal showing all capital market trades, interest, dividends, and corporate action benefits for a financial year.  FAQs are available on the income tax portal (WEB).  It details investments and income from various sources, helping taxpayers verify transactions before filing ITRs. Discrepancies may arise due to the estimated cost of acquisition being based on the best available price (possibly showing closing prices instead of actual transaction prices).  See blog.quicko.com/decoding-the-new-annual-information-statement for more information.


Where can the trades that are taken for a particular period be seen? - Trades for a specific period are found in the Tradebook on Console. To download it, log in to console.zerodha.com, click Reports, then Tradebook, select the segment and date range, and click the arrow. Download in XLSX or CSV format.  Use the Symbol tab to view trades for individual stocks and the Tags tab to filter by tags.  The Tradebook heatmap also shows trades (see "What does the Trade book heat map on Console represent?"). Note: Equity (external trades) include trades from corporate actions, IPOs, OFS, buybacks, and transfers between brokers; MF (external trades) include NFO trades and transfers between brokers; and Tradebook can only be downloaded for a 365-day period.

How to download the interest statement? - Log in to console.zerodha.com, click Funds, then Interest statement, select the date, click View, and then click Download CSV.

What is the online DIS marker in the trade book on Console? - The online DIS marker in Console's trade book indicates that a sell trade was settled using online delivery instructions (instead of a physical Delivery Instruction Slip).  Zerodha uses online processes; the online DIS consent allows for online debit instructions.  Trades settled this way are tagged with "online DIS" in the trade book.

What is Verified P&L and how to use it? - Verified P&L on Console lets you publicly share your profit and loss report via a shareable link. To generate a link: On mobile, log in to console.zerodha.com, tap the context menu, Account, then Verified P&L; select display name, image, description, date range, whether to show trades and segments, and click Save; copy the link. On web, log in, click Account, then Verified P&L; follow the same steps and click Enable public page, then copy the link. The link shows Net Realised P&L (after deducting charges), a heatmap, longest profitable streak, and most profitable day.  The report is tamper-proof. Transferred securities aren't included. You can regenerate the link or switch to private mode.  Personal data is not shown. See tradingqna.com/t/fake-pnl-of-live-trading-finfluencers-scam/152081/34 for more information.



Are any physical documents sent by Zerodha via mail or courier? - Zerodha does not send physical documents unless specifically requested by the client (e.g., requesting physical annual reports via a ticket). Clients may receive physical annual reports from companies whose shares they hold. To switch from physical to digital annual reports, create a ticket.

How to convert Console reports to PDFs? - Open the XLSX or CSV report in Excel or a spreadsheet program. Go to File, then Export, then Create PDF. Select the save location.  This works for Holdings, P&L, Tradebook, Tax P&L, and other reports.

Can Zerodha provide reports in either softcopy or hardcopy format with a seal and signature? - Yes, create a ticket to request softcopies of P&L, Tax P&L, Funds statement, SOT, and SOH reports with a seal and signature.  Charges are ₹50 + 18% GST for up to 10 pages, and ₹5 per additional page + 18% GST. Hard copies have an additional ₹100 + 18% GST courier charge.  P&L, Tax P&L, and Funds statements can be downloaded without a seal and signature from Console (see links provided in text for instructions).  See "What is a statement of transaction (SOT) and how do I interpret the same?" and "What is the statement of holdings (SOH) and how to interpret the same?" for SOT and SOH download instructions.



How to download the GST invoice for the charges posted on the funds statement? - On Console (WEB), click Reports, then Downloads, select Invoice under the Statement tab, choose the month, year, and company, and click Download.  Note: GST is only applicable to some charges on the funds statement; it does not apply to Delayed payment charges, STT, and Stamp duty.

Why did CDSL or NSDL deposit money to my bank account? - CDSL or NSDL may deposit money into your bank account for several reasons: 1) Interest on Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) - SGBs pay 2.5% annual interest, credited twice yearly; 2) Dividends; 3) Partial entitlement during corporate actions (bonus issues, stock splits) where cash is given instead of fractional shares; 4) Interest from State Development Loans (SDLs).  See zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/government-securities for more on G-secs.



What is Zerodha’s referral programme, and what are its benefits? - Zerodha's referral program rewards you with 300 reward points for each successful referral (a new account opened using your referral link within 60 days).  Brokerage-based referral commissions are suspended until further notice from the exchange (as of August 25, 2024).  Reward points can be used to waive AMC or subscribe to paid partner products; they don't expire and are non-refundable. You can also use the referral link at zerodha.com/refer.  The referral must open an account within 60 days of registration; referrals won't be credited if the prospect registered on the website before using the referral link. Check console.zerodha.com/refer for immediate confirmation.  The referral wallet is blocked for violations of terms and conditions (see zerodha.com/tos/referrals). Referral benefits apply to new accounts from January 1, 2020.  Minors can refer, receiving only 300 reward points.

Who is an Authorised Person (AP) and how to register as an AP with Zerodha? - According to SEBI (WEB), an Authorised Person (AP) is an individual, firm, LLP, or corporate body appointed by a stockbroker to act on their behalf.  SEBI doesn't register or charge APs; they're approved by the stock exchange (NSE charges ₹5000 per segment + GST).  APs are supervised by the stockbroker and exchange; they can't handle client funds or securities directly. To appoint an AP, a stockbroker submits an application to the exchange.  Eligibility criteria for individuals include Indian citizenship, age 18+, no fraud/dishonesty convictions, good reputation, at least 10th-standard education, and relevant certification.  For non-individuals, all partners/directors must meet individual criteria, the entity's MoA must include securities business, and sufficient infrastructure is required.  Conditions include the stockbroker's responsibility for AP actions, no direct client interaction by the AP, remuneration solely from the stockbroker, and written agreements between the stockbroker and AP. To register as a Zerodha AP: Be an existing Zerodha client; have an organic lead source (no paid advertising or trade inducement); have at least 100 successful referrals via Zerodha's referral program; create a ticket providing contact information, lead source, entity type, and business nature.  You'll receive a response within two business days.



Do the reward points expire? - No, reward points do not expire.  They can be accumulated and used to subscribe to Zerodha partner products (see console.zerodha.com/refer); they are non-refundable. Note: Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), brokerage-based referral commissions are temporarily suspended.  You will still receive 300 reward points for each successful referral.


How to become a Zerodha Partner? -  Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), the brokerage-based referral commission aspect of the Zerodha Partner program is temporarily suspended.  To be considered for partnership, you must have organically referred at least 100 accounts (through online or offline means, without misinformation or incentives like cashbacks), and Zerodha will contact you to verify your referrals.  See zerodha.com/tos/referrals for terms and conditions.



If the old referral account is closed and reopened, will it be considered for the referral benefit? - No, if an old referral account is closed and reopened, it will not receive referral benefits.  Referral benefits apply to new accounts opened since January 1, 2020.  Note: Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), brokerage-based referral commissions are temporarily suspended.  You will still receive 300 reward points for each successful referral.

See zerodha.com/tos/referrals for terms and conditions.  To check referral status, log in to console.zerodha.com, click your Client ID, then Rewards & referrals, and finally View Referrals. Note: Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), brokerage-based referral commissions are temporarily suspended.  You will still receive 300 reward points for each successful referral.


Why are withdrawal requests not being processed under the brokerage sharing program? - Withdrawal requests may not be processed if: The referrals were added before January 2020; or one or more referral accounts were opened in the current month (only the previous month's referrals are considered for payouts).  If you have a referral this month but not last month, you can request a withdrawal the following month. See the Terms & Conditions for Referral Incentive Scheme Policy for details. Note: Due to exchange regulations (as of August 25, 2024), brokerage-based referral commissions are temporarily suspended.  You will still receive 300 reward points for each successful referral.

Can Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) invest in mutual funds through Coin? - Yes, provided they have an NRI account with Zerodha.  See "What documents are required to open a Zerodha account as an NRI?" for account opening information.  Note: US and Canada-based investors cannot invest in mutual funds through Coin.

What is Coin? - Coin is a platform for buying mutual funds online directly from asset management companies with no commission.  Assets (mutual funds, stocks, currencies, bonds) are held in your demat account.  Learn more at coin.zerodha.com; the app is available on Android and iOS.



Can non-individual account holders invest in mutual funds through Coin? - Yes, using NEFT or RTGS. To pay: Click Buy, enter the amount, click Buy now, then Confirm; make the payment via netbanking using the account details shown on Coin. Funds are transferred on a FIFO (First In First Out) basis; excess funds are refunded within T+4 days.  Funds must be from a bank account linked to your Zerodha account; IMPS transfers are rejected; NAV allocation depends on ICCL settlement (up to 24 hours); HDFC netbanking transfers are instant; current accounts can be used; one transfer can cover multiple orders, but not vice versa; and orders are open in BSE StARMF for T+5 days. The account details on Coin are unique: MFDICC006498ABXXXX (MFDICC = ICCL initials, 006498 = Zerodha's member code, ABXXXX = client login).



What are Direct Mutual Funds? - Direct mutual funds let investors buy funds directly from the Asset Management Company (AMC), bypassing distributors and their commissions, resulting in lower costs and potentially higher returns.  An AMC (Asset Management Company) or fund house invests pooled funds into various financial instruments.  A distributor is an intermediary between the investor and the AMC, earning commissions.  Bypassing the distributor in direct plans means you avoid paying these commissions.  See "Why is the NAV for direct mutual funds higher than regular mutual funds?" for more details.



How to pledge mutual fund investments to get collateral margins? - Pledging mutual funds is the same as pledging other securities. See "How to pledge securities to get collateral margin?" for instructions.



What are the charges applicable for investing in securities through Coin? - There are no charges for investing in mutual funds, ETFs, and mutual fund NFOs through Coin. There are also no DP (Depository Participant) charges.  There are no additional Account Maintenance Charges (AMC) for using Coin because investments are held in demat form.



What are the advantages of using Coin? - Coin offers commission-free investing in direct mutual funds (avoiding the commission expense added to regular plans' expense ratios); step-up SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) features; easy SIP management (start, pause, stop, adjust amounts); NAV order tracking and a wide selection of AMCs and funds; a single portfolio view of stocks and mutual funds (easily pledged for loans); consolidated statements for tax deductions; easier claims by dependents in case of death; and the ability to view fund investments and compare mutual funds.  See "What are Direct Mutual Funds?" and "What is step-up SIP, and how can it be set on Coin web?" for more details.


What is the difference between Coin and Console mandates? - Coin mandates automatically transfer funds from your bank account to the BSE StAR MF ICCL account for SIP orders. Console mandates automatically transfer funds from your bank account to your Zerodha account for stock investments, ETF SIPs, etc.  Coin mandates cannot be used for Console transactions, and vice versa.  Both types of mandates can transfer up to ₹1 crore.  See "What is a Mandate and how to create them for SIPs on Coin app?" and "How to set up automatic fund transfers from a bank account to a Zerodha trading account?" for more details.



How to check the mandate status on Coin? - Click Mandates on Coin. After registration, the status will show as Processing; within 3 business days, it will update to Successful or Failed.  Failed mandates are removed and cannot be tracked.



Why is the mandate registration status not updated on Coin? - e-mandate registration usually takes 5 business days.  If Zerodha doesn't receive bank confirmation, the status remains pending.  Zerodha follows up with banks periodically, but a specific timeline for verification can't be provided because it depends on the bank.



Why can the Coin mandate registration not be completed? -  If your browser's pop-up blocker is enabled, the mandate creation page may not load. To disable it: In the Chrome Android app, click the context menu (⋮), Settings, Site settings, Pop-ups and redirects, and toggle the button to allow pop-ups; In Chrome web, click the context menu (⋮), Settings, Privacy and security, Pop-ups and redirects, and click "Sites can send pop-ups and use redirects". For Mozilla, see support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/pop-blocker-settings-exceptions-troubleshooting.



Why did the Coin mandate registration fail? - A Coin mandate registration may fail due to: Intermittent issues on the bank's or NPCI's end (retry the registration);  Digio disabling certain banks (the list changes); authentication failure (unsuccessful netbanking/debit card authentication, closing the window before entering credentials, or incorrect credentials).  Note: Failed mandates are removed and can't be tracked.



What are the charges for Coin mandates? - There are currently no charges for Coin mandate registration. However, banks may charge penalties for insufficient funds (amounts vary).  Mandate verification charges also vary by bank (a list of charges per bank is provided in the text; some banks do not charge).



Can clients switch between two different schemes of the same AMC on Coin? - Clients cannot directly switch between schemes within the same AMC on Coin.  However, they can redeem from one fund and then purchase another within the same AMC. Note: This is considered a switch; even without funds being credited to your bank account, capital gains tax still applies.



How to activate Coin? - Coin is activated by default for all Zerodha demat account holders.  It may be inactive if: Your Zerodha account was recently opened (activation takes up to 24 hours automatically); your account was opened before September 15, 2015 (switch your demat account from IL&FS to Zerodha - see "How to switch demat account from IL&FS to Zerodha?"); or you opened a Zerodha trading account without a demat account (open a demat account - see "How do I open a demat account if I already have a trading or commodity account?").  Note: Order placement is disabled if your PAN isn't linked to Aadhaar (see "How to link PAN with Aadhaar?").



What does IDCW on Coin mean? - IDCW stands for Income Distribution Capital Withdrawal, indicating a dividend distribution plan in mutual funds. Dividends are partial payouts of profits; the NAV decreases after payout. See "What is the impact of dividends on the NAV if the Income Distribution Capital Withdrawal (IDCW) scheme has paid dividends?" for more information.  Note: IDCW reinvestment schemes are not currently available on Coin.



Is stamp duty applicable for mutual fund purchases on Coin? - Yes, stamp duty of 0.005% is applicable and adjusted with the units allotted; it's not a separate charge.  For example, a ₹10,000 investment would have a ₹0.50 stamp duty, reducing the investment to ₹9,999.50 and affecting the number of units allotted accordingly. Note: Stamp duty isn't currently displayed under charges on Console but is expected to be available soon.

How long will it take for mutual fund units to show up in the demat account? - For liquid schemes, units are settled by 7 PM on T day and visible on Console by T+1 day. For non-liquid schemes, units are settled by 7 PM on T+1 day and visible on Console by T+2 day.  See "What is the cut-off time for mutual fund transactions on Coin and what is the applicable NAV?" for NAV and cut-off information. Note: There may be late deliveries (see "Why are the newly allotted units shown as NA on the Coin app?").



How to add a nominee for mutual fund holdings on Coin? - Since Coin mutual funds are held in demat form, the nominee for your demat account also applies to your mutual funds; you don't need to add a separate nominee for mutual funds. See "How do I add a nominee online in Zerodha?" for instructions on adding a demat nominee.  Check your nominee details at console.zerodha.com/account/nominee.  Ignore any AMC communication about nomination if a nominee is already added to your demat account.



Why are investments made on Coin not visible on the AMC website? - Coin investments are in demat form, while AMC websites only show folio-based investments.  Also, if your mobile number or email isn't updated with the RTA, you won't be able to log in. See "Why are the email id or mobile number registered with the AMC different from Coin?".


Why is the minimum initial investment for SIPs in some schemes higher on Coin? - Coin processes SIPs as lump-sum investments on your chosen SIP dates. AMCs (fund houses) set minimum initial investment amounts (for the first investment) and minimum additional purchase amounts (for subsequent investments).  Coin's minimum SIP amount may be higher than on the AMC site because of the AMC's minimum initial investment requirement.  For example, if the minimum initial investment is ₹5000 and the minimum additional purchase amount is ₹1000, your first SIP investment must be ₹5000 or more, while subsequent investments can be ₹1000 or more.  To avoid this initial investment requirement, use AMC SIPs (set up directly through Coin).  Minimum initial investment amounts vary across AMCs and schemes.





Why are clients unable to log in to the AMC website to check their investments? - Investments made through Coin are held in demat form and may not be visible on the AMC website (it's at the AMC's discretion whether to show demat investments).  You can check your investments on Coin and on your CDSL demat holding statements (downloadable from CDSL Easi - see "How to download transaction cum holding (SOT and SOH) statement?").  Note: ELSS statements can be downloaded on Coin (see "What are ELSS funds, and how can the ELSS statement be downloaded?").



How to change email ID or mobile number registered with the AMC for Coin investments? -  The email and mobile number registered with the AMC are the same as your Zerodha details, also shared with CDSL (the depository) and the RTA (Registrar and Transfer Agent). To change them, follow the same process as changing your Zerodha details (see "How to change the registered mobile number or email address with Zerodha online?"). Note: RTAs update their database on weekends; your demat account nominee also applies to Coin investments (see "How to add a nominee to the Zerodha account online?").



Why were the funds not automatically debited as per the Coin SIP schedule? - Funds may not be debited even if your SIP is linked to a mandate if: There is insufficient opening balance in your bank account on the transaction (T) day (only the T-day opening balance is considered, funds added on T day don't count); or the bank rejected the fund transfer (contact your bank).





What does exit load mean and how to calculate it for mutual fund investments? - Exit loads are penalties for early redemption of mutual funds.  The exit load is calculated on the NAV (Net Asset Value) at the time of redemption, based on the factsheet's exit load percentage for the purchase month.  For example: If you invested ₹50,000 at a NAV of ₹50 (receiving 1000 units) and redeem at a NAV of ₹60 with a 1% exit load, the exit load is (1% of ₹60) * 1000 units = ₹600; you receive ₹59,400 (₹60,000 - ₹600). See zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/the-mutual-fund-fact-sheet for more about factsheets.



What is the impact of dividends on the NAV if the Income Distribution Capital Withdrawal (IDCW) scheme has paid dividends? - The NAV decreases by the dividend amount. For example, if the NAV is ₹15 and a ₹5 dividend is paid, the NAV after the payout will be ₹10.



How to buy Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs)? - On the Kite app: Tap Bids, then Govt. securities, then Place bid, then Place bid again, and finally Submit. On Kite web: Log in to kite.zerodha.com, click Bids, then Govt. securities, then Place bid; enter the amount and click Place bid.  Note:  Kite Bids are for the primary market; allotment takes up to 15 days after the offer closes, and it may take another 15 days to appear in holdings after listing; SGBs from the Kite marketwatch (secondary market) appear in holdings on T+2 day; an email confirms order status; funds are debited on the last day of the order window (credits from same-day stock sales aren't included); only individuals, HUFs, and trusts can buy in the primary market; and fractional unit refunds are credited within 5-6 days of allotment.



What are ELSS funds, and how can the ELSS statement be downloaded? - ELSS (Equity-Linked Savings Schemes) are Indian equity mutual funds offering tax benefits under Section 80C (up to ₹1,50,000 deduction).  Investments are via SIP or lump sum; there's a 3-year lock-in period; and profits are taxed as LTCG (Long-Term Capital Gains).  To download the ELSS statement: Log in to coin.zerodha.com, click Mutual funds, then ELSS statement, and select the financial year; or log in to console.zerodha.com/dashboard, click Reports, then Downloads, select ELSS statement, choose the financial year, and click Download.  (Units appear on T+2 day).  See "What is an SIP?" and "What is a lump-sum investment?" and "How does taxation work for Mutual Fund investments?" for more details.


Where can clients learn more about investing in mutual funds and Coin? - For video tutorials, see "Mutual Funds Investing: A Step-by-Step Guide".  Varsity's "Introduction to Mutual Funds – Varsity by Zerodha" provides basic information.  For more details on mutual funds and Coin, visit Coin Direct MF and the Mutual Fund & ETFs category on Trading Q&A.



What is an SIP? - A Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) is a method of investing regular, smaller amounts of money at intervals (weekly, monthly, quarterly, etc.) instead of a single lump sum. This helps mitigate market volatility by buying more units at low prices and fewer at high prices. See "How to create a SIP on the Coin app?" and "How to create a stock SIP on Kite?" for instructions.



What are Scheme Information Document (SID), and where can they be read? - A Scheme Information Document (SID) contains details about a mutual fund scheme (investment objectives, style, costs, allocation, risks). To find it on Coin, open the mutual fund details page, scroll down, and click Scheme document.  (Instructions for app and web versions are shown visually in the original text but not described in words).



What does NAV mean? - NAV (Net Asset Value) is the per-share price of a mutual fund or ETF. It's calculated daily by dividing a fund's total assets minus liabilities by the number of outstanding shares.  It represents the value of one share if the fund's assets were liquidated and liabilities paid. Investors buy and sell units at the NAV.  See zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/concept-of-fund-nav for more information.


How does taxation work for mutual fund investments? -  Taxation depends on whether the fund is equity or non-equity (see table in original text for LTCG and STCG rates based on fund type and holding period).  Consult a Chartered Accountant before filing returns.  Note:  Dividends from non-equity schemes are paid after a 28.84% DDT (Dividend Distribution Tax); growth schemes are preferable in this case.  See "What are Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) and Short-Term Capital gains (STCG), and how are they calculated?" for more on LTCG and STCG.



What is Expense ratio in mutual funds and when is it charged? - The expense ratio is the fee charged by mutual funds for managing your investments; it's a percentage of the AUM (Assets Under Management).  It's deducted from the NAV before the daily NAV is announced and is disclosed monthly in the factsheet on the AMC's website.  Direct plans have lower expense ratios than regular plans. See tradingqna.com/t/how-costly-are-regular-mutual-funds-compared-to-direct-plans/63599/3 for more information.



Mutual funds for minor accounts - FAQs:

Q. Can minors invest in mutual funds through Coin? - Yes.  See "What is the Coin login ID and how to log in to the Coin app?" for login instructions.

Q. Which bank can be used to complete the payment on Coin? - Currently, only the minor's Zerodha-linked bank account; the exchange will soon allow the guardian's account.

Q. Which payment modes are supported for completing the payments in Coin? - UPI, netbanking, NEFT, RTGS; SIPs can be linked to mandates for auto-debit.

Q. Where are the funds from mutual funds redemption credited in a minor account? - The minor's Zerodha-linked bank account; requests from other accounts are rejected.

Q. Can the payment be completed using the guardian's bank account? - Currently no, only the minor's linked account; the exchange will soon allow the guardian's account.

Q. Can minors initiate SIPs (Systematic Investment Plans) through Coin? - Yes. See "How to create a SIP on the Coin app?" for instructions.

Q. Can all the mutual funds be purchased through a minor account on Coin? - Yes.

Q. Can mutual funds be transferred to the minor's account? - Yes, using CDSL easiest.

Q. Where can the mutual funds transferred to the minor's Zerodha account be tracked? - On Coin and Console.

Q. Are there any restrictions on Coin for minor accounts? - No.

Q. What should be done when the minor turns 18? - Convert the account to an individual account. See "How can a minor account be converted to an individual account?".

Q. Who is liable to pay the taxes (if applicable) for a minor account? - The guardian.

Q. Are there any additional fees or charges associated with maintaining a minor account on Coin? - No.


Why are mutual fund investments displayed under Kite holdings? - Close-ended mutual funds transferred to a Zerodha account appear in Kite holdings because they're exchange-traded.  Non-exchange-listed close-ended funds are visible on Console under Holdings. See "What are open ended and closed ended funds?" for more on fund types. Note: You cannot invest in close-ended mutual funds through Coin.



Why is the NAV for direct mutual funds higher than regular mutual funds? - Regular funds have higher expense ratios than direct funds because they pay commissions to brokers/distributors.  The expense ratio is deducted from the fund's assets before calculating the NAV.  Therefore, a higher expense ratio (like in regular funds) results in a lower NAV compared to direct funds, which have lower expense ratios. See "Introduction to Mutual Funds – Varsity by Zerodha" for more on mutual funds.



How to redeem fractional units of Liquidbees? - Fractional Liquidbees units cannot be sold directly. You can transfer them to another demat account via CDSL easiest (see "How can I register for CDSL Easiest using my Zerodha demat account?"). To redeem them, you can either: Transfer them to the AMC's demat account using CDSL Easiest (details for Nippon India and DSP Mutual Funds are provided in the text); or fill out a Redemption Request Form (RRF) (PDF), send a soft copy via ticket for verification, and courier the form to Zerodha (address provided in the text). Redemption proceeds are credited to your linked Zerodha bank account. Note: Only fractional units are redeemed; whole units are returned to your demat account.





What does lock-in period mean? - The lock-in period is the time you can't redeem mutual fund units; it applies to ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) and retirement funds.  ELSS funds have a 3-year lock-in; retirement funds have a 5-year lock-in or until retirement.  See "What are ELSS funds and how will it help me in tax planning?".  The lock-in period is shown under holdings.



What does CAGR mean? - CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate) measures the annual growth rate of an investment over a period, considering compounding. It calculates the constant rate of return needed to reach the current value from the initial investment.  Unlike average annual return, it accounts for compounding, providing a smoother representation of returns over time. See zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/the-stock-markets (point 6.7) for more details.


What are open ended and closed ended funds? - Open-ended funds have no limit on the number of shares they can issue; buying creates new shares, selling removes them from circulation; shares are bought/sold on demand at the daily NAV (Net Asset Value). Closed-ended funds have a fixed number of units; you can't buy units after the NFO (New Fund Offer) period; they raise capital once through an NFO; and their stock price fluctuates based on market forces and the value of their holdings.



How to get in touch with Zerodha Fund House? - Create a ticket on their website or check their FAQs at help.zerodhafundhouse.com/support/solutions.


Why does the mutual fund NAV display T-2 day value on Console? - Console displays the T-2 day NAV because NAV announcement times vary by scheme type (equity: 9 PM T-day; liquid: 11 PM T-day; international: 1:30 PM T+1 day). Data vendors receive and update data by the next morning; the mutual fund Bhav copy is generated at 3 PM T+1 day. Console calculates P&L using this data on the night of T+1 day, so the T+2 day holdings reflect the T-day NAV accurately.  Note: Coin shows holdings based on the T-1 day NAV.



How to calculate mutual fund returns? -  Several methods exist, depending on the investment type and duration:

* **Case 1: Lump sum investment, less than a year:** Use Absolute Return.  Absolute Return % = (Current Value - Investment Value) / Investment Value x 100.

* **Case 2: Lump sum investment, over multiple years:** Use CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate). CAGR = [(Current Value / Investment Value)^(365/Number of Days)] - 1. See the provided link for more on CAGR.

* **Case 3: SIP (Systematic Investment Plan), less than a year:** Use XIRR (Extended Internal Rate of Return).

* **Case 4: SIP, over a year:** Use XIRR.

See the provided Varsity link for detailed mutual fund return calculations.



Is GST included in the mutual fund expense ratio? - Yes, GST is included in the mutual fund expense ratio and doesn't need to be paid separately because money management is a service under GST purview.



What does exit load mean and how to calculate it for mutual fund investments? - Exit loads are penalties charged by AMCs for early mutual fund redemptions. The exit load is a percentage of the NAV (Net Asset Value) at the time of redemption, as specified in the factsheet for the month of purchase.  For example: If you invested ₹50,000 at a NAV of ₹50 (getting 1000 units) and redeem at a NAV of ₹60 with a 1% exit load, the exit load is (1% of ₹60) * 1000 units = ₹600, leaving a redeemable amount of ₹59,400.  See zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/the-mutual-fund-fact-sheet for more on factsheets.


Can Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) invest in mutual funds through Coin? - Yes, but only if they have a Zerodha NRI account. For information on opening an NRI account, see "What documents are required to open a Zerodha account as an NRI?".  Note that US and Canada-based investors cannot invest through Coin due to compliance reasons.

What is Coin? - Coin is an online platform for buying mutual funds directly from asset management companies, with no commission fees.  All your assets (mutual funds, stocks, currencies, bonds) are held and accessible in your demat account. For more information, visit coin.zerodha.com.  The Coin app is available on the Android Play Store and iOS App Store.

Can non-individual account holders invest in mutual funds through Coin? - Yes, using NEFT or RTGS.  To pay, click Buy, enter the amount, click Buy now and Confirm; then make the payment via netbanking using the account details shown on Coin. Funds are transferred on a FIFO (First In First Out) basis; excess is refunded within T+4 days. Funds must come from a linked Zerodha bank account; IMPS transfers are rejected; NAV allocation depends on ICCL settlement (up to 24 hours); HDFC netbanking is instant; current accounts are accepted; one transfer covers multiple orders (but not vice versa); and orders remain open in BSE StARMF for T+5 days.  The Coin account details are unique: MFDICC006498ABXXXX (MFDICC = ICCL initials, 006498 = Zerodha's member code, ABXXXX = client login).



What are Direct Mutual Funds? - Direct mutual funds allow investors to buy mutual funds directly from the AMC (Asset Management Company) or fund house, without using a distributor. This eliminates distributor commissions and fees, leading to lower costs and potentially higher returns.  An AMC invests pooled funds from multiple investors into various financial instruments. A distributor acts as an intermediary between the investor and the AMC, earning a commission (e.g., a ₹1000 investment might have ₹10 deducted for the distributor). Direct plans avoid this commission, leading to higher returns compared to regular plans. See "Why is the NAV for direct mutual funds higher than regular mutual funds?" for more information.


How to pledge mutual fund investments to get collateral margins? - Pledging mutual funds is done the same way as pledging other securities.  For instructions, see "How to pledge securities to get collateral margin?".

What are the charges applicable for investing in securities through Coin? -  There are no charges for mutual funds, ETFs, or mutual fund NFOs.  There are also no DP (Depository Participant) charges.  There are no additional Account Maintenance Charges (AMC) because Coin investments are held in demat form.  See "What does Depository Participant(DP) charge mean?" and "What is Account Maintenance Charge (AMC) with regard to my demat account at Zerodha?".



What are the advantages of using Coin? - Coin offers commission-free investing in direct mutual funds (avoiding commissions added to regular plans' expense ratios); step-up SIP features (automatic SIP amount increases); easy SIP management (start, pause, stop, adjust amounts); NAV order tracking with a wide fund selection; a single portfolio view of stocks and mutual funds (easily pledged for loans); consolidated statements simplifying tax deductions; easier claims by dependents in case of death; and the ability to view and compare fund investments.  See "What are Direct Mutual Funds?" and "What is step-up SIP, and how can it be set on Coin web?" for more details.


What is the difference between Coin and Console mandates? - Coin mandates automate fund transfers from your bank account to your BSE StAR MF ICCL account for SIPs. Console mandates automate fund transfers from your bank account to your Zerodha account for stock investments and ETF SIPs.  They are not interchangeable; a Coin mandate cannot be used for Console, and vice versa.  Both types of mandates can handle up to ₹1 crore.  See "What is a Mandate and how to create them for SIPs on Coin app?" and "How to set up automatic fund transfers from a bank account to a Zerodha trading account?" for more details.


How to check the mandate status on Coin? - Click on "Mandates" on Coin. After registration, the status will be "Processing"; within 3 business days it will change to "Successful" or "Failed". Failed mandates are removed and can't be tracked.



Why is the mandate registration status not updated on Coin? -  e-mandate registration usually completes within 5 business days.  However, if Zerodha doesn't receive confirmation from your bank, the status will remain pending.  Zerodha can't give a specific timeframe for verification because it depends on the bank; they periodically follow up with the banks involved.



Why can the Coin mandate registration not be completed? - A browser's pop-up blocker may prevent the mandate creation page from loading. To fix this: In the Chrome Android app, click the three vertical dots (⋮), then Settings, Site settings, Pop-ups and redirects, and toggle the button to allow pop-ups; In Chrome web, click the three vertical dots (⋮), then Settings, Privacy and security, Pop-ups and redirects, and select "Sites can send pop-ups and use redirects". For Mozilla Firefox instructions, see support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/pop-blocker-settings-exceptions-troubleshooting.



Why did the Coin mandate registration fail? -  Possible causes include: Intermittent problems on the bank's or NPCI's website (try again later); Digio disabling certain banks from mandate registration (check for updates to the list of disabled banks); or authentication failure (due to unsuccessful netbanking/debit card authentication, closing the authentication window prematurely, or entering incorrect credentials).  Note that failed mandates are removed and can't be tracked on the mandate page.


What are the charges for Coin mandates? - There are no charges for registering Coin mandates. However, banks may charge penalties for insufficient funds (amounts vary by bank).  Banks also charge mandate verification fees (a list of fees per bank is provided in the original text; some banks do not charge).



Can clients switch between two different schemes of the same AMC on Coin? - No, clients cannot directly switch between schemes of the same AMC on Coin.  However, they can redeem from one scheme and then purchase another within the same AMC.  This is still considered a switch and is subject to capital gains tax, even though the funds aren't credited to your bank account.



How to activate Coin? - Coin is usually activated automatically for all Zerodha demat account holders.  However, there are some situations where it might be inactive:  If your Zerodha account was recently opened (it may take up to 24 hours for automatic activation); if your account was opened before September 15, 2015 (you'll need to switch your demat account from IL&FS to Zerodha – see "How to switch demat account from IL&FS to Zerodha?"); or if you opened a Zerodha trading account without a demat account (you need to open a demat account – see "How do I open a demat account if I already have a trading or commodity account?"). Note:  Order placement requires a PAN linked to Aadhaar (see "How to link PAN with Aadhaar?").


What does IDCW on Coin mean? - IDCW stands for Income Distribution Capital Withdrawal, meaning it's a dividend distribution plan.  Mutual fund dividends are partial profit payouts from underlying investments; the NAV (Net Asset Value) decreases after the payout. For the impact of dividends on NAV, see "What is the impact of dividends on the NAV if the Income Distribution Capital Withdrawal (IDCW) scheme has paid dividends?".  Note:  Dividends are trackable on the AMC website; IDCW reinvestment isn't currently available on Coin.



Is stamp duty applicable for mutual fund purchases on Coin? - Yes, a 0.005% stamp duty applies. It's adjusted with the units allotted and not charged separately. For example, a ₹10,000 investment would have a ₹0.50 stamp duty, resulting in 999.95 units allotted at a NAV of 10. Note that stamp duty isn't currently shown under charges on Console, but this is expected to change soon.


How long will it take for mutual fund units to show up in the demat account? -  The time it takes for mutual fund units to appear in your demat account depends on the scheme type: Liquid schemes settle by 7 PM on T-day and are visible on Console by T+1 day; Non-liquid schemes settle by 7 PM on T+1 day and are visible by T+2 day. See "What is the cut-off time for mutual fund transactions on Coin and what is the applicable NAV?" for more on NAV and cut-off times. Note that there may be delays; see "Why are the newly allotted units shown as NA on the Coin app?" for more information.


How to add a nominee for mutual fund holdings on Coin? - Because Coin mutual funds are held in demat form, the nominee you've added to your demat account also applies to your mutual funds; you don't need to add a separate nominee for them.  See "How do I add a nominee online in Zerodha?" for instructions on adding a demat nominee.  To check your nominee information, go to console.zerodha.com/account/nominee. Ignore any AMC nomination requests if a nominee is already assigned to your demat account.


Why are investments made on Coin not visible on the AMC website? -  Coin investments are held in demat form, while AMC websites typically only show folio-based investments.  Additionally, if your mobile number or email address isn't updated with the RTA (Registrar and Transfer Agent), you won't be able to log in to the AMC website. See "Why are the email id or mobile number registered with the AMC different from Coin?" for more information.



Why is the minimum initial investment for SIPs in some schemes higher on Coin? - Coin treats SIPs as lump-sum investments made on your chosen SIP dates.  AMCs (Asset Management Companies) set minimum initial investment amounts (for the first investment) and minimum additional purchase amounts (for subsequent investments).  Coin's minimum SIP amount might be higher than on the AMC website because of this minimum initial investment requirement. For example, if the minimum initial investment is ₹5000 and the minimum additional purchase amount is ₹1000, your first SIP must be ₹5000 or more, while subsequent SIPs can be ₹1000 or more.  To avoid the higher initial investment, use AMC SIPs (set up directly via Coin).  Minimum initial investment varies across AMCs and schemes.



Why are clients unable to log in to the AMC website to check their investments? - Investments made through Coin are held in demat form and may not appear on the AMC website, as it's up to the AMC whether to display demat investments. You can track these investments on Coin and via your CDSL demat holding statements (downloadable from CDSL Easi; see "How to download transaction cum holding (SOT and SOH) statement?").  ELSS statements are also downloadable on Coin (see "What are ELSS funds, and how can the ELSS statement be downloaded?").



How to change email ID or mobile number registered with the AMC for Coin investments? - Your AMC email and mobile number are the same as your Zerodha details, also recorded by CDSL (the depository) and shared with the RTA (Registrar and Transfer Agent). Why were the funds not automatically debited as per the Coin SIP schedule? -  Your SIP must be linked to a mandate for automatic debits. If not linked, no debit request is generated. Even if linked, debits may fail due to insufficient funds (only the opening balance on the transaction day is considered; funds added that day don't count) or bank rejection (contact your bank for details).  For example, a ₹5,000 SIP on April 5th requires sufficient funds by April 4th; adding funds on April 5th won't suffice.



What does exit load mean and how to calculate it for mutual fund investments? - Exit loads are small penalties AMCs charge for early mutual fund redemptions. The exit load is a percentage of the NAV (Net Asset Value) at redemption, as stated in the factsheet for the investment month. For example: A ₹50,000 investment at a NAV of ₹50 (1000 units) redeemed at a NAV of ₹60 with a 1% exit load would have an exit load of (1% of ₹60) * 1000 units = ₹600, resulting in a redemption of ₹59,400. For more on factsheets, see zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/the-mutual-fund-fact-sheet.


What is the impact of dividends on the NAV if the Income Distribution Capital Withdrawal (IDCW) scheme has paid dividends? - The NAV of an IDCW (Income Distribution Capital Withdrawal) scheme will decrease by the amount of the dividend paid. For example, if the NAV before a ₹5 dividend is ₹15, the NAV after the dividend will be ₹10.

How to buy Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs)? - **On the Kite app:** Tap Bids, then Govt. securities, then Place bid, then Place bid again, and finally Submit.  **On Kite web:** Log in to kite.zerodha.com, click Bids, then Govt. securities, then Place bid; enter the amount and click Place bid.  **Important notes:** Bids from the Govt. securities section on Kite are for the primary market. Allotment takes up to 15 days after the offer closes, with an additional 15 days possible before they appear in Kite holdings. SGBs bought from Kite marketwatch (secondary market) appear on T+2 day after delivery.  An email confirms order status. Funds are debited on the last day of the order window (same-day stock sale credits are not considered). Only individuals, HUFs (Hindu Undivided Family), and trusts can buy in the primary market (corporates, partnerships, LLPs, and NRIs cannot). Fractional unit refunds are credited to your primary Zerodha-linked bank account or Zerodha account within 5-6 days of allotment.


What are ELSS funds, and how can the ELSS statement be downloaded? - ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Schemes) are diversified Indian equity mutual funds offering tax benefits under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, 1961 (up to ₹1,50,000 deduction).  They're purchased via SIP or lump sum and have a 3-year lock-in period.  Profits are taxed as LTCG (Long-Term Capital Gains). What is an SIP? - An SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) is a way to invest smaller amounts of money regularly (weekly, monthly, or quarterly) in mutual funds or the stock market, instead of investing a large sum at once.  This helps reduce the risk of market volatility because you buy more units at lower prices and fewer at higher prices.  For creating mutual fund SIPs, see "How to create a SIP on the Coin app?". What does NAV mean? - NAV (Net Asset Value) is the per-share price of a mutual fund or ETF.  It's calculated daily by subtracting the fund's liabilities from its assets, then dividing by the number of outstanding shares.  It represents the value of one share if the fund's assets were sold and liabilities paid.  It's the price at which investors buy and sell fund units. For more information, visit zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/concept-of-fund-nav.



How does taxation work for mutual fund investments? -  Taxation of mutual funds depends on whether it's an equity or non-equity fund and the holding period (see the table in the original text for LTCG and STCG rates).  This information is for retail individual investors only and is subject to change; consult a Chartered Accountant (CA) before filing taxes.  Dividends from non-equity schemes are paid after a 28.84% DDT (Dividend Distribution Tax), so growth schemes are generally preferred. For more on LTCG and STCG, see "What are Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) and Short-Term Capital gains (STCG), and how are they calculated?".



What is Expense ratio in mutual funds and when is it charged? - The expense ratio is the fee a mutual fund charges for managing your money; it's a percentage of the AUM (Assets Under Management). It's deducted from the NAV before the daily NAV is announced and is shown monthly in the factsheet on the AMC's website.  Direct plans have lower expense ratios than regular plans. Q. Can all mutual funds be purchased through a minor account on Coin? - Yes.

Q. Can mutual funds be transferred to a minor's account? - Yes, using CDSL easiest.

Q. Where can mutual funds transferred to a minor's Zerodha account be tracked? - On Coin and Console.

Q. Are there any restrictions on Coin for minor accounts? - No.

Q. What should be done when the minor turns 18? - Convert the account to an individual account. See "How can a minor account be converted to an individual account?".

Q. Who is responsible for paying taxes (if applicable) for a minor account? - The guardian.

Q. Are there additional fees or charges for a minor account on Coin? - No.


Why are mutual fund investments displayed under Kite holdings? - Close-ended mutual funds that have been transferred to your Zerodha account will show up in Kite holdings because they are traded on the exchange. If a close-ended fund isn't listed on an exchange, it won't appear in Kite but can be found under Holdings on Console. To learn more about the difference between open-ended and closed-ended funds, see "What are open ended and closed ended funds?". Note that you can't invest in close-ended funds through Coin.


Why is the NAV for direct mutual funds higher than regular mutual funds? - The difference in NAV between direct and regular mutual funds comes down to the expense ratio.  The expense ratio is the fee paid to the fund house for managing investments.  This expense is deducted from the fund's assets before calculating the NAV. Regular funds have higher expense ratios than direct funds because they pay commissions to brokers and distributors.  Therefore, the higher expense ratio in regular funds leads to a lower NAV compared to direct funds. For a comprehensive understanding of mutual funds, see "Introduction to Mutual Funds – Varsity by Zerodha".

How to redeem fractional units of Liquidbees? -  You can't sell fractional Liquidbees units in the secondary market.  Instead of redeeming them directly, you can transfer them to another demat account using CDSL easiest (see "How can I register for CDSL Easiest using my Zerodha demat account?"). To redeem them, you have two options:

**Online:** Transfer the fractional units to the AMC's demat account using CDSL Easiest. (Demat account details for Nippon India Mutual Fund and DSP Mutual Fund are provided in the original text). See "How to register for CDSL Easiest using the Zerodha demat account?".

**Offline:** Complete and submit a Redemption Request Form (RRF) (PDF). Send a soft copy via a ticket for verification. Once confirmed, courier the form to Zerodha at the address provided in the original text.

Redemption proceeds are credited to your primary Zerodha-linked bank account.  Note that only the fractional portion is redeemed; whole units are returned to your account.

What does lock-in period mean? - A lock-in period is the time you can't redeem mutual fund units. This applies to ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) and retirement funds. ELSS funds have a 3-year lock-in period, while retirement funds have a 5-year lock-in or until retirement, whichever comes later. For more information on ELSS funds, see "What are ELSS funds and how will it help me in tax planning?". The lock-in period is shown in your holdings.


What does CAGR mean? - CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate) is a financial term representing the average annual growth rate of an investment over a specific period, accounting for compounding. It determines the constant yearly return needed to reach the final value from the initial investment value. Unlike a simple average annual return, CAGR considers the effect of compounding, providing a more accurate long-term return. For more information, see zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/the-stock-markets, point 6.7.


What are open ended and closed ended funds? - **Open-ended funds:** These funds don't have a limit on the number of shares they can issue; buying creates new shares, selling removes them. Shares are bought and sold on demand at their NAV (Net Asset Value), calculated daily based on the fund's underlying securities.  **Closed-ended funds:** These funds have a fixed number of units.  Once the NFO (New Fund Offer) period is over, investors can no longer buy units. They raise a set amount of capital once through an NFO, issuing a fixed number of shares which investors buy like stocks. The share price fluctuates based on market forces (supply and demand) and the value of the fund's holdings.


How to get in touch with Zerodha Fund House? - For questions about Zerodha Fund House, you can create a ticket on their official website (link provided in the original text) or find answers in their FAQs at help.zerodhafundhouse.com/support/solutions.


Why does the mutual fund NAV display T-2 day value on Console? - The Console shows the T-2 day NAV because mutual fund NAV announcement times vary depending on the scheme type (equity schemes: 9 PM on T-day; liquid schemes: 11 PM on T-day; international underlying schemes: 1:30 PM on T+1 day). Data vendors get the data from AMFI and update it the following morning.  The mutual fund Bhav copy is generated at 3 PM on T+1 day, which Console uses to compute the mutual fund P&L that night. Therefore, on T+2 day, the Console holdings show the T-day NAV for accuracy.  Note that Coin shows holdings based on the T-1 day NAV.



How to calculate mutual fund returns? - The method for calculating mutual fund returns depends on whether it's a lump sum investment or an SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) and the investment duration:

**Lump Sum Investments:**

* **Less than one year:** Use Absolute Return:  (Current Value - Investment Value) / Investment Value * 100

* **More than one year:** Use CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate): [(Current Value / Investment Value)^(365/Number of Days)] - 1  (See the provided link for more information on CAGR).

**SIP Investments:**

* **Less than one year:** Use XIRR (Extended Internal Rate of Return).

* **More than one year:** Use XIRR.

For detailed information on calculating mutual fund returns, refer to the Varsity link provided in the original text.


Is GST included in the mutual fund expense ratio? - Yes, GST is included in the expense ratio and is not charged separately.  Since fund management is a service provided by the AMC (Asset Management Company), it's subject to GST.

What does exit load mean and how to calculate it for mutual fund investments? - Exit loads are penalties applied by Asset Management Companies (AMCs) to discourage early withdrawals from mutual funds. The exit load is calculated as a percentage of the Net Asset Value (NAV) at the time of redemption.  The specific percentage is defined in the factsheet for the month the investment or SIP was made.  To learn more about factsheets, visit zerodha.com/varsity/chapter/the-mutual-fund-fact-sheet.

**Example:**  A ₹50,000 investment with a NAV of ₹50 results in 1000 units. If the investor redeems these 1000 units when the NAV is ₹60 and the exit load is 1%, the calculation is: (1% of ₹60) * 1000 units = ₹600. The net amount received would be ₹59,400 (₹60,000 - ₹600).
